extracted.intended_audience: auditors of states, local governments, Indian tribal governments, institutions of higher education, and nonprofit organizations performing OMB A-133 (single) audits; federal agency grant managers and pass-through entities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and performing single audits under OMB Circular A-133, identifying compliance requirements that could have a direct and material effect on federal programs and providing audit objectives and suggested audit procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix of Compliance Requirements (Part 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Matrix of Compliance Requirements identifies the Federal programs and compliance requirements addressed by this Supplement and associates programs with applicable types of compliance requirements. Boxes contain 'Y' where a type may apply or are shaded if the program normally does not have activity subject to that requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a 'Y' is present the auditor should use Part 3 (and Parts 4 or 5 if applicable) to plan tests of compliance. A 'Y' does not automatically require testing at a particular entity; auditors exercise professional judgment to determine applicability and materiality. Use the matrix to quickly determine which compliance requirement types to consider for each program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities Allowed or Unallowed (Part 3, A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance requirement addressing whether costs/activities charged to the program are permitted under statutes, regulations, and award terms — i.e., activities allowed or unallowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 3 provides the audit objective and suggested audit procedures for determining whether expenditures/activities are allowable. Auditors must consider program-specific restrictions in Part 4 or award agreements. Auditor judgment is required to determine sufficiency of suggested procedures; the Supplement is not a 'safe harbor' for procedures but may be a 'safe harbor' for identifying requirements if auditors perform reasonable procedures to ensure currency and supplementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable Costs/Cost Principles (Part 3, B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements applying cost principles to determine which costs are allowable, reasonable, and allocable to federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 3 lists the audit objective and suggested procedures to test cost allocation, allowability, and reasonableness. Auditors should refer to applicable cost principles (e.g., OMB Circular A-87/A-122 or successor rules) and award terms, and perform inquiry and document review to identify contract/grant-specific cost provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash Management (Part 3, C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for proper management of cash disbursements and drawdowns, ensuring federal funds are requested, held, and disbursed in accordance with program rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested audit procedures in Part 3 address testing of drawdowns, timing of requests, and bank/accounting records. Auditors should assess whether funds are drawn only as needed, reconciled, and whether interest or other requirements apply; consider program-specific guidance in Part 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis-Bacon Act (Part 3, D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with prevailing wage requirements where applicable — i.e., the Davis-Bacon Act provisions for construction wages under federal programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 3 provides audit objectives and suggested procedures related to payroll, certified payrolls, and wage determinations. Auditors should verify payroll records, wage determinations, and compliance with certified payroll reporting as applicable to the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (Part 3, E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements that beneficiaries, participants, or entities receiving program benefits meet program-specific eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit objectives and suggested procedures include testing sample eligibility determinations, documentation, and controls over screening/enrollment. Auditors must examine program rules in Part 4/award documents to identify specific eligibility criteria and any exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and Real Property Management (Part 3, F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for acquisition, management, use, disposition, and recordkeeping for equipment and real property purchased with federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 3 provides objectives and suggested tests (inventory, tagging, usage, disposal, property records). Auditors should review property records, verify physical existence, and confirm compliance with retention, title, and disposition rules; consult Part 4 for program-specific property rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching, Level of Effort, Earmarking (Part 3, G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for matching or cost-sharing contributions, maintenance of effort or level-of-effort provisions, and earmarking restrictions on how funds must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested procedures address verification of matching contributions, determination of whether level-of-effort requirements are met, and compliance with earmarking. Auditors should review supporting documentation for match, assess calculation methods, and ensure any earmarked funds are used as required by statute/award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of Availability of Federal Funds (Part 3, H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements regarding the time period when federal funds may be obligated and expended — i.e., obligational and disbursement cutoff rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 3's audit objective and suggested procedures address testing that obligations and expenditures occurred within the authorized period. Auditors should review cut-off procedures, examine transactions around period-ends, and consider grant award dates and extensions. Part 6 internal control guidance emphasizes controls, communications, and cut-off reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement and Suspension and Debarment (Part 3, I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements that procurement actions comply with the A-102 Common Rule or OMB Circular A-110 (as applicable), ensure full and open competition, proper documentation, and that contractors/subrecipients are not suspended or debarred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested audit procedures include review of procurement files, vendor selection documentation, cost/price analyses, and verification against the GSA List of Parties Excluded. Part 6 provides internal control characteristics (procurement manuals, segregation of duties, vendor exclusion checks, retention of procurement documentation). Auditors should also check for required certifications for subawards/contracts over thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income (Part 3, J)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for identification, recording, and allowable use of program income generated by federal programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 3 supplies audit objectives and suggested procedures to test earning, recording, depositing, and use of program income in accordance with program rules. Part 6 control guidance recommends pricing/collection policies, recording mechanisms, reconciliations, and monitoring; auditors should examine accounting systems, deposit records, and program income usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Property Acquisition and Relocation Assistance (Part 3, K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements under the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act (URA) for acquisition, appraisal, negotiation, and relocation assistance when programs involve real property acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested audit procedures include review of acquisition and relocation files, payments, and documentation of compliance with URA. Part 6 internal control guidance emphasizes written policies, trained staff, documentation systems, and management monitoring of relocation and acquisition activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting (Part 3, L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements that financial and performance reports filed with Federal agencies/pass-through entities include all activity for the reporting period, be supported by records, and be fairly presented per program requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit objectives and suggested procedures focus on verifying report accuracy against accounting/performance records, supervisory review, and timeliness. Controls include tracking systems for report due dates, use of general ledger as source, staff competence, and periodic comparison of reports to supporting records (Part 6 guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient Monitoring (Part 3, M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements that pass-through entities identify award information and applicable compliance requirements to subrecipients, monitor subrecipient compliance, resolve audit findings, and ensure subrecipients obtain required audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 3 describes audit objectives and suggested procedures for assessing pass-through entity monitoring (e.g., reviewing award documents, tracking subrecipient audits, site visits, follow-up on findings). Part 6 provides detailed internal control characteristics: establishing tone at the top, documented monitoring procedures, risk assessment of subrecipients, tracking systems, and corrective action processes. Auditors should verify agreements include CFDA info, requirements, subrecipient acknowledgments, and that the pass-through entity enforces audit requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Tests and Provisions (Part 3, N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program-unique compliance requirements, tests, and provisions that are specific to individual Federal programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Special Tests and Provisions vary by program, Part 3 does not include generic audit objectives or procedures; auditors must refer to Part 4 (Agency Program Requirements) for program-specific objectives and suggested procedures. For programs not included in the Supplement, auditors should follow Part 7 guidance to identify program-specific special tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Program Requirements (Part 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand-alone sections for each Federal program included in the Supplement that describe program objectives, program procedures, and compliance requirements specific to that program. Special Tests and Provisions (and their audit procedures) for each program are included here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors shall use Part 4 to obtain program-specific compliance criteria and to supplement the general compliance requirement types in Part 3. Because program operations may vary by award, auditors must obtain an understanding of the non-Federal entity's actual program procedures and review award/grant agreements for additional contract-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clusters of Programs (Part 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on grouping closely related programs (e.g., Research & Development, Student Financial Aid, other clusters) treated as a single program for A-133 audit purposes because of similar compliance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 5 provides compliance requirements, audit objectives, and suggested audit procedures for clusters (notably R&D and Student Financial Aid). Auditors should determine whether programs administered by an entity form a cluster by referring to Part 5 and award documents and then plan/testing accordingly treating the cluster as one program for major program determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Control (Part 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristics of internal control intended to provide reasonable assurance of compliance with the types of compliance requirements in Part 3. Internal control is addressed via six components: Control Objectives, Control Environment, Risk Assessment, Control Activities, Information and Communication, and Monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 6 is neither mandatory nor all-inclusive but provides practical internal control characteristics for each compliance type. Auditors must obtain an understanding of a non-Federal entity's internal control sufficient to plan tests to support an assessed level of control risk; testing of internal control should be designed case-by-case. Part 6 includes example control objectives and specific control environment/risk assessment/control activity/communication/monitoring examples for each compliance area (e.g., procurement, program income, reporting, subrecipient monitoring, period of availability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Auditing Programs Not Included in this Compliance Supplement (Part 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions to assist auditors in identifying compliance requirements and designing tests of compliance for federal programs not included in the Supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 7 directs auditors to use the types of compliance requirements in Part 3 to identify applicable requirements for programs omitted from the Supplement and to design appropriate audit procedures. Auditors should perform inquiry of management and review award documents and applicable statutes/regulations to determine program-specific requirements.
